payload.description:
`make app` in demo/Makefile says "pre-build the standalone runner (do this first; it is the slow one)" but runs:

    cd muster-ui && nix build 'path:.#default' --out-link .run/app

That is `packages.default`. `make run` launches with `nix run 'path:.'`, which is `apps.default`. Resolved on 2026-08-13, they are different derivations:

    packages.default      -> /nix/store/03n3y6r187...-logos-muster_ui-module
    apps.default.program  -> /nix/store/q4gpjhnqal...-run-logos-standalone-ui/bin/run-logos-standalone-ui
    .run/app symlink      -> /nix/store/03n3y6r187...-logos-muster_ui-module

So `make app` out-links the .lgx module and returns in seconds, then `make alice` starts building the standalone runner -- which pulls lez_core and with it the RISC Zero proving stack from Rust source. Measured: 827 cargo-package derivations and still going at 36 minutes. The target's whole purpose is defeated, and its name (.run/app) points at something that is not the app.

Compounding it: nix defaults to max-jobs = 1 and there is no nix.conf here setting otherwise, so that build runs strictly serially -- 41 derivations/min at load 2.5 on a 16-core machine. Relaunching with NIX_CONFIG='max-jobs = 8' took it to roughly 110/min.

Fix, two parts:
1. Point `make app` at the runner. The flake already demonstrates the trick at flake.nix:81-82 -- `packages.exchange` interpolates `base.apps.${system}.default.program`, so building it warms the runner into the store. Either reuse that or expose a `packages.runner` for the standalone app derivation and out-link that.
2. Have the demo pass --max-jobs (or document it in RUNBOOK.md), so a first launch on a cold store is not an hour of one-at-a-time crate builds.

Found while launching two peers to confirm the LEZ retraction work (exo-fb8). Not related to that change -- it is pre-existing.

payload.description:
Observed in the two-peer run on 2026-08-13 (alice -> bob, credited successfully).

A shielded payee has no address to watch, so there is nothing to subscribe to -- the money is found by scanning with the viewing key. That part is the design, not a defect (see GAPS.md 4b). What is missing is that nothing in the app performs that scan on the payee's behalf.

Evidence: bob's chat_ui log after 10:20 contains nothing but health probes. He made no transfer, so no settleAfterTransfer runs for him, and there is no periodic wallet poll anywhere in the backend -- the only repeating timer is m_healthProbe (ChatBackend.cpp:221). His balance moved only when a human pressed Refresh.

The trigger should be the conversation, which is where the news already arrives. The sender posts a send-receipt card, and the payee's client already parses it: ChatBackendJourney.cpp:151 and ChatBackendIntent.cpp:145 both branch on type == "send-receipt" to fold it into the journey. Nothing on that path touches the wallet. Proposed: when an inbound send-receipt names a rail whose destination is a holding this wallet owns, kick refreshBalances() -- or better, the settleAfterTransfer poll loop, since the payee faces the same 'accepted but not yet visible' lag the sender does.

Honesty constraint, which is why this is not just 'call refresh': a receipt is authenticated in the room but the zone checks none of it (see the authorization claim in VisibilityClaims.qml). The receipt may therefore trigger a *scan*, because a scan only looks -- but the UI must never render 'you were paid' on the receipt's word. It must show what the scan actually found, and say nothing if the scan found nothing yet.

Fallback if the automatic trigger is deferred: a visible affordance on the private holding telling the payee that money is found by scanning and that Refresh is how they do it. Right now a payee who was told 'I sent it' sees an unchanged balance and no explanation, which is indistinguishable from the payment having failed -- the same confusion that produced the withdrawn report in exo-fb8.

Not a regression from exo-fb8; it is a gap that work revealed. Consider disclosing it in GAPS.md and the payment claim once the behaviour is decided.

Upstream bug in logos-co/logos-chat-module, pinned at dfe8ccf3 (2026-08-04) in demo/muster-ui/flake.lock. Found 2026-08-14 while designing pre-populated demo state.

SYMPTOM. Every launch of a peer starts with no conversations, and its chat address is different. Measured across three sessions -- alice sees bob as 3096fd24, then 0a91a0ca, then b3f8b3be; bob sees alice as e58fc481, then 36681062, then 55cbb48c. A conversation created and used with messages exchanged, followed by a clean shutdown (chat_module 'shutdown' called, app exit code 0), is gone on relaunch. Reproduced twice.

CAUSE. Persistence is implemented but not used. chat_module_plugin.so contains a full SQLite layer:

    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO conversations (local_convo_id, remote_convo_id, convo_type) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)
    SELECT local_convo_id, remote_convo_id, convo_type FROM conversations
    SELECT name, secret_key FROM identity WHERE id = 1
    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO identity (id, name, secret_key) VALUES (1, ?1, ?2)
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ephemeral_keys (...)

plus ratchet_state and skipped_keys tables, and the error string 'host did not assign an instance persistence path; start the host with a session or config dir'. The contract says so too (chat_module.lidl:69): 'Storage lives under the instance directory the host assigns; init fails when the host assigned none.'

But the binary also contains ':memory:', and no named database filename -- the only .db/.sqlite strings are SQLite's own internals (temp.sqlite, vacuum_db.sqlite, anon.db). No database file is created anywhere on the filesystem during a session; a search of the whole home dir over a session window found nothing. chat_module logs 'init: state installed' on every start and logs nothing at shutdown. The connection is opened in memory, so the schema is created fresh each run and discarded at exit.

Inference to flag: ':memory:' in a strings dump is not proof of the connection string in use. But combined with no file on disk, no named db filename, 'state installed' every init, and demonstrably non-surviving identity, the case is strong. Confirming it needs the module source, which we do not have checked out.

NOT CONFIGURABLE. ChatConfig has two optional fields, delivery_preset and log_level. Nothing about storage.

IMPACT ON US.
1. No pre-populated demo state is possible for conversations. Wallet state is ours and persists fine (module_data/chat_module/<instance>/muster-wallet/*.json); the conversation cannot be snapshotted at all, because even restored messages would name addresses that no longer exist.
2. An identity that changes every restart means a peer address shared out of band -- which is what create_conversation consumes -- is only valid for one session.

NEXT. Report upstream with this evidence, the way the LEZ findings went. Ask whether the in-memory open is deliberate for the testnet build or an oversight, and what it would take to point it at the instance persistence path the host already assigns.

Related: exo-d0f, exo-d6d.

payload.body:
Retracted the ':memory:' inference while drafting the upstream report. SQLite is statically linked into chat_module_plugin.so (609 sqlite3_ symbols, amalgamation version strings), so ':memory:' is present in any binary bundling SQLite regardless of the connection string in use. It is not evidence of anything.

What survives, and is stronger than what it replaced: the module is launched with --instance-persistence-path and writes its own log into exactly that directory every run, so the path is assigned, exists and is writable — and no database appears there or anywhere else. And the binary contains 'SELECT name, secret_key FROM identity WHERE id = 1', which has no purpose unless identity is meant to be reloaded across runs.

Draft report for the developers: demo/poc/BUG-chat-module-state-not-persisted.md. It is written to be corrected rather than accepted — §3 lists five things we cannot determine from outside, including whether delivery_preset 'logos.test' selects ephemeral storage, which would explain the whole thing.

Answered upstream 2026-08-14. Confirmed, and it is not our bug and not configurable: persistence is not implemented for lambdaAccounts + lambdaChat, all conversations and identities are ephemeral. It was implemented for pairwise conversations and regressed on the pivot to DeMLS; held deliberately until group state is stable, to cut down on forked groups and state desync.

Tracking: logos-messaging/libchat#28. Roadmap: installation management, 2026 chat beta.

None of our five hypotheses was right — not the logos.test preset, not the standalone host, not a build feature, not a derived path. The SQL we found in the binary is residue of the pairwise implementation that regressed: the tables are compiled in, nothing calls them under DeMLS.

Method note worth keeping: reading capability out of a shipped binary tells you what the code once did, not what it currently does. A dead path and a live one look identical in a strings dump.

Reported from use, 2026-08-14: starting the 'pay someone' flow posts an address-request card in the sender's own thread as though the ask happened, but the receiver is never asked.

MECHANISM. ChatBackend.cpp:753 (and :756 for the 'request' verb) fires requestAddress(convoId) from applyConversationCreated, as soon as the *local* conversation exists. But create_conversation only sends the cryptographic invite -- the peer has not joined the MLS group yet. The card is therefore sent into a group of one: chat_module accepts it, emits message_sent, applyMessageSent renders it locally, and the sender sees 'Asked for an address' with nothing having been asked.

This is not a delivery delay. The message is encrypted to an MLS epoch the peer was never a member of, so it cannot be read by them once they join either. Store-node catchup cannot help.

Our own doctest already works around exactly this, at doctests/exchange/run-exchange.mjs:132: 'create_conversation sends only the cryptographic invite; wait until Alice has joined (her conversation list shows it) before Bob's first message, so the message reaches her subscribed thread rather than racing ahead of her join'. It waits by watching the RECEIVER. The app cannot do that.

WHY THERE IS NO EASY FIX. The sender has no signal that the peer joined a direct conversation:
- GroupMember.pending is documented as never set for a direct conversation -- chat_module.lidl:104, 'A direct conversation reports both participants and never a pending one'. So the roster looks complete from the instant it is created.
- delivery_state_changed(delivery_state, detail) is transport-wide -- it is the Status record's field, alongside convo_count -- not a per-message receipt. There is no way to learn whether a given message landed.
- members_changed may or may not fire for a direct conversation when the peer commits. NOT VERIFIED; needs a live two-peer run to establish, and it is the one thing that could make a clean fix possible.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
1. Hold the card until there is evidence the conversation is two-way, and say so on screen ('waiting for them to join') rather than sending into the void. Honest, and works without a signal, but the wait is unbounded and the demo's first move becomes a spinner.
2. Retry the send on a timer for ~60s. Needs no signal, but the peer may end up with two address requests, and it still cannot confirm.
3. Wait on members_changed, if it fires. Cleanest if it works -- verify first.
4. Do not auto-send at all: land the user in the conversation with the ask ready to send by hand. Least magic, least wrong.

Whichever we pick, the sender's card must stop asserting an ask that did not happen -- that is the part that is actively misleading, and it is the same class of error as a receipt for a payment nobody made.

WORTH REPORTING UPSTREAM regardless: there is no way for a sender to know a direct conversation is ready to carry a message, and no per-message delivery state. Either would make this solvable at the app layer. Related to the notes in poc/BUG-chat-module-state-not-persisted.md.

payload.title: ADR-013: build muster-ui on a basecamp-coherent builder (exo-c6a workaround)

payload.body: ADR-013 (exo-193) filed as the non-upstream unblock path: build muster-ui on a basecamp-coherent builder instead of muster_module's Nim-cdylib builder, keeping this issue for the upstream logos-cpp-sdk 4b66dac0 codegen bump. The two are parallel — either one unblocks the P4 render; ADR-013 does not wait on upstream. Spec in docs/02-implementation-plan.md ADR-013.

SPIKE finding 1 — exo-c6a's rev table has ROTTED (platform moved since 2026-08-20). Cross-checked flake.locks today:
- basecamp's recorded exo-c6a values are gone: view-module-runtime '1fde7d43' appears in NEITHER basecamp's nor the local builder's lock anymore. basecamp now pins module-builder rev 4717b9af35d8.
- cpp-sdk '4b66dac0' and view-runtime '3c3735c2' now appear in BOTH basecamp's and the local nim-cdylib builder's dependency graphs; cpp-sdk 'e3744fb8' (exo-c6a's builder value) is in the local builder's graph but NOT basecamp's.
- both locks carry MANY nodes per input (nested graph), so 'the' effective rev can't be read from lock text alone — must eval or inspect built artifacts to get the rev the ui-host actually links.
IMPLICATION: the specific pins in ADR-013 (4b66dac0 / 1fde7d43) are illustrative, already stale, and must be RE-MEASURED against current basecamp. The ADR's *approach* is unaffected and in fact more rot-resistant: 'follow basecamp's builder (currently 4717b9af)' beats 'pin these exact revs'. Also note: ui/flake.lock is gitignored (machine-local path inputs) and currently absent.

SPIKE finding 2 — MECHANISM VALIDATED (source trace of logos-module-builder). The core ADR-013 assumption holds:
- The typed modules().muster_module.* client is generated + compiled by the CONSUMING UI module's builder (A), NOT the module's builder (B). buildCppPlugin.nix:221-226; intent at mkLogosModule.nix:170-174.
- It reads only muster_module's published .lidl output (packages.<sys>.lidl); for a cdylib module that's a straight copy of committed muster.lidl (mkLogosModule.nix:791-795). The module is PARSED, never rebuilt (Q4). Precondition: muster_module must expose the 'lidl' output — it does (interface cdylib + codegen.lidl). If it ever stops, consumer falls into a transitional header path that DOES rebuild the dep + re-couples (common.nix:141-213).
- Client + view-glue compile against the UI builder A's OWN cpp-sdk/qt-sdk/protocol pins (buildCppPlugin.nix:111-131, 207-218). => build muster-ui under basecamp's builder and its view-glue ABI-matches basecamp's ui-host.

CORRECTION to exo-c6a: logos-view-module-runtime is NOT a plugin compile input at all — it's threaded only into logos-standalone-app (runtime host). exo-c6a's 'view-runtime skew' was a red herring for the compile; the compile-relevant roots are cpp-sdk/qt-sdk/protocol. The fix is 'build the UI under basecamp's builder', not 'pin view-runtime'.

VERDICT: spike (a) GREEN on mechanism. Concrete next step: set ui/flake.nix logos-module-builder to basecamp's current builder (4717b9af), nix build .#lgx, install into a basecamp --user-dir, render under xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, assert health()->ok. Remaining risks are runtime-only: bus string-marshalling (exo-526) and libsecp256k1 RUNPATH — only the build+run reveals them.

SPIKE finding 3 — BUILD GREEN (actual build, not just source trace). Set ui/flake.nix logos-module-builder to basecamp's builder 4717b9af (dropping the follows=muster_module coupling); nix build ./ui#lgx exited 0. Log proves the mechanism:
  Running logos-cpp-generator (api-style=qt)...
  Generating deps from LIDL: muster_module
  Generated dependency wrapper: muster_module_api.h (class MusterModule, 6 methods, 0 events)
  logos-module-builder: generating ui plugin glue (muster_ui)...
=> the coherent builder generated the typed muster_module client (all 6 methods) from its .lidl + compiled the view-glue, producing logos-muster_ui-module.lgx (716KB, variant linux-amd64-dev). muster_module was READ (logos-muster_module-lidl.drv, a copy), NOT rebuilt — confirming Q4. Generators pulled from cache.nix.logos.co (substituter works for this box). This is the exact build exo-c6a blocked under the cdylib builder.

CAVEAT: build-green != render-works. exo-c6a's std::bad_alloc was at RUNTIME view instantiation in basecamp's ui-host, not at build. The build proves compile-ABI-compat; the decisive test is still the RENDER — install the .lgx into a basecamp --user-dir (dev variant), load under xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, drive via logos-qt-mcp, assert health()->ok + the re-materialization strip. Remaining runtime risks unchanged: bus marshalling (exo-526), libsecp256k1 RUNPATH. ui/flake.nix edit held local (not committed) pending render verification.

SPIKE finding 4 — RENDER: ADR-013 core PROVEN, secp blocker fixed. Baked muster into logos-basecamp installedDev (via muster's own pre-built .install outputs — basecamp's installDev re-bundle of .lib fails with 'qml/Main.qml not found', a bundler-version skew; the standalone install is self-consistent). Ran basecamp offscreen + logos-qt-mcp driver. RESULT:
  ui-host: loaded plugin "muster_ui" from ".../muster_ui_plugin.so"  <-- NO std::bad_alloc
=> the coherent-built muster_ui view-glue INSTANTIATES in basecamp's ui-host. This is exactly the exo-c6a crash, GONE. ADR-013's core claim is proven at runtime.

The render still failed end-to-end, but for an ORTHOGONAL reason = exo-c6a's F1 (secp256k1), not ADR-013: muster_module failed to load ('libsecp256k1.so.5: cannot open shared object file'). logos_host UNSETS LD_LIBRARY_PATH for module subprocesses (confirmed: unsetenv(LD_LIBRARY_PATH) in the binary), so env injection can't fix it — only the plugin's own RUNPATH. Dead module -> health() times out (20s) -> ui-host never signals ready -> view not shown.

FIXED F1 properly (the 'real fix' exo-c6a named) in the module-builder: nim.link libs (metadata codegen.nim.link, e.g. secp256k1) now get their nix lib dirs appended to the plugin's INSTALL_RPATH. Edits: lib/mkLogosModule.nix passes -DLOGOS_MODULE_NIM_LINK_RPATHS=<runtimePkgs lib dirs>; cmake/LogosModule.cmake appends them to INSTALL_RPATH ('$ORIGIN:<dir>'). Verified: ldd now resolves libsecp256k1.so.5 via RUNPATH, no LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This is a general builder fix (any Nim module with external FFI libs), a clean contribution back like PR #202. Rebuilding basecamp to re-run the full render.

SPIKE COMPLETE — ADR-013 PROVEN END-TO-END. logos-qt-mcp driver in basecamp (offscreen): 2 passed, 0 failed.
  ✓ muster_ui: the view instantiates and renders (header + composer visible) — the exo-c6a bad_alloc is GONE
  ✓ muster_ui: muster_module.health() marshals to ok — exo-526 clean on the coherent chain
The coherent-built UI renders in basecamp's ui-host AND the real muster_module engine loads + responds. This is the running, visible, real-engine Muster UI that exo-c6a blocked, achieved WITHOUT the upstream codegen fix.

Three changes made this work (across three repos):
1. muster/ui/flake.nix (COMMITTABLE, the ADR-013 fix): logos-module-builder.url pinned to basecamp's builder 4717b9af, dropping follows=muster_module. muster_module stays an input only for its .lidl (typed client codegen), built by its own cdylib builder. => client + view-glue compile against basecamp-coherent cpp-sdk/qt-sdk, ABI-match the ui-host.
2. logos-module-builder (UPSTREAM, needs PR — like #202): the secp/nim.link RUNPATH fix. mkLogosModule.nix passes -DLOGOS_MODULE_NIM_LINK_RPATHS=<runtime lib dirs>; LogosModule.cmake appends to INSTALL_RPATH. Fixes non-bundled hosts (logoscore). NOT enough for basecamp — see #3.
3. logos-basecamp (TEST-ONLY): co-locate libsecp256k1.so.5 in modules/muster_module/ (). basecamp's app.nix strips external module RUNPATH entries (removeReferencesTo, keeps only $ORIGIN) + logos-core unsets LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so the rpath fix alone is stripped away; only a co-located .so survives. The real upstream fix belongs in the builder (stage nim.link .so files INTO the module dir, not just rpath) OR basecamp should stop stripping module rpaths — both are follow-ups.

NEXT: commit muster/ui/flake.nix; file the module-builder rpath+co-location fix upstream; note the basecamp rpath-stripping as a separate upstream issue. exo-c6a can stay open for the upstream codegen path, but ADR-013 is a working unblock TODAY.

P4 acceptance harness LANDED at ui/tests/muster-ui-test.mjs (+ README). Drives muster-ui in basecamp via logos-qt-mcp, offscreen: 3/3 green — render, health()->ok, and propose->real re-materialization strip (module re-derives the EIP-712 safeTxHash from the effect; describe() shows the real 2-of-3 Safe on chain 31337). Screenshot artifact captured (muster-ui.png). README documents the app-under-test provisioning (local basecamp bake-in + secp co-location) until the two supporting fixes land upstream.

payload.description: Re-validate the stack table against upstream HEADs, then decide build-vs-consume logos-chat-module. Deciding questions: (1) curve conflict — is chat-module identity Ed25519 while Muster signs secp256k1, at current HEAD? (2) does its membership model re-key forward PROVABLY (F-16), and can we VERIFY not just trust it? (3) does it leak signer identity (FS-7)? (4) persistent identity — logos_chat::open() mints an unpersisted account; is there an IdentityStore the facade skips? Also confirm logos-delivery-module's API (content topics, pub/sub with delivery events, store queries) still matches ADR-006. Note: local clone is logos-chatsdk-module; demo pins github:logos-co/logos-chat-module/v0.2.2 — reconcile the naming.
payload.title: ADR-010: resolve chat-module build-vs-consume (P3 decision gate)

payload.body: RESOLVED: BUILD Muster's epoch layer for F-16; consume only logos-delivery-module (ADR-006). Code-level investigation of logos-chat-module v0.2.2 + libchat (logos-messaging, pinned 5c55c2ee 2026-07-26). Naming: local logos-chatsdk-module is a stale unrelated C++ thing, NOT a rename; real crypto core is logos-messaging/libchat. Findings: (Q1 curve) identity is Ed25519/X25519, secp256k1 only transitive via alloy — no binding to Muster's secp256k1 Safe key; F-9 intersection would need a binding libchat doesn't provide. (Q2 F-16) groups are DeMLS/openmls; joiner forward-secrecy is INHERITED+TRUSTED from MLS with NO libchat test proving the negative; member REMOVAL not implemented at all (no remove_member in core/conversations or chat_module.lidl) — removal half of F-16 absent. (Q3 FS-7) MLS leaf credential binds a stable identity+Ed25519 key to every message/commit; message_received surfaces directory-verified sender — no unlinkable mode; anonymous driver deanonymized. (Q4 persistence) PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false, openmls on MemoryStorage — ephemeral, can't survive R-4/R-6 restart; IdentityStore exists in core/sqlite but facade doesn't use it. (Q5 delivery) confirms ADR-006: content topics, publish, subscribe, storeQuery, reliable channels; embeds its own Waku node. Decision recorded in plan ADR-010.

payload.description: Define the Transport interface (F-15: content topics, publish with delivery/propagation events, subscribe, store queries, channels) in module/src/transport/, plus a local/in-memory implementation for integration tests (working agreement: tests use local transport, never mock it). The delivery_module-backed impl (consume logos-delivery-module via the logos API) follows once the interface + local impl are proven. Codes against the interface; delivery binds at runtime (ADR-006). Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: Transport interface + local/in-memory impl

payload.body: DONE: Transport interface + in-memory LocalTransport committed (7dea6a8), 5/5 tests (live exchange, deterministic content address, offline catchup via store, idempotent ingest R-2/R-4, topic isolation). module/src/transport/transport.nim + tests/transport_test.nim.

payload.description: Wire the delivery-backed Transport by consuming logos-delivery-module over the logos API. BLOCKER/scope: there is no Nim caller-side SDK — inter-module calls go through the lp_* C ABI from logos-protocol, which the logos-rust-sdk binds (~2145 lines: binds lp_*, serializes params, drives callback trampolines, delivers results over channels; Client::bind(name)->LogosModuleSDK.plugin(name)). Need a Nim binding of the lp_* subset for delivery's 4 methods (createNode/start/subscribe/send) + the messageReceived/connectionStateChanged events, then a DeliveryTransport: Transport impl over it. muster_module declares delivery_module as a dependency (metadata.json). This is the caller-side analog of muster_gen's callee-side codegen. Depends on exo-c8b (interface, done). Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: delivery-backed Transport (Nim lp_* outbound-call binding + delivery client)

payload.body: Delivery-backed Transport BUILT (binding validated end-to-end). module/src/transport/lp_ffi.nim mirrors the rust-sdk src/ffi.rs (~12 lp_* extern decls: lp_client_create/lp_invoke/lp_invoke_async/lp_subscribe/lp_string_free/… + the {"_bytes":"<base64url,unpadded>"} bstr codec from bytes.rs). module/src/transport/delivery.nim = DeliveryTransport : Transport over it (publish=lp_invoke send, subscribe=lp_invoke subscribe + lp_subscribe messageReceived event routing, storeQuery best-effort). VERIFIED: (1) both type-check; (2) the lp_* symbols are exported (T) in liblogos_protocol.a which muster_module already links; (3) the module PLUGIN builds+links with lp_protocol_version() called from describe() — the FFI resolves in the real plugin. So my earlier '2145-line Nim SDK' framing was wrong: it's a small FFI over the same C ABI both SDKs bind, no Rust needed. REMAINING (next increment): wire Transport into the coordination flow (multi-instance), a live two-instance test over a real delivery node, harden the messageReceived callback's foreign-thread GC seam (storage-nim abandoned-flag pattern), and switch send to lp_invoke_async (sync send blocks the dispatch thread on delivery's accept handshake, per the chat module).

payload.description: Build the per-conversation epoch layer (ADR-002 default): a symmetric epoch key encrypts envelopes (AEAD, libsodium); the epoch key is ECIES-wrapped to each member's secp256k1 pubkey (reusing the Safe key, recovered from their signatures — no second curve). Re-key on every membership change: add -> new epoch, joiner gets only the new key (can't decrypt earlier epochs, F-16 forward secrecy); remove -> rotate, removed member can't read new epochs. F-16 acceptance test: a member added mid-conversation provably cannot decrypt earlier epochs (verify, not trust — the ADR-010 bar). Builds against LocalTransport. DONE so far: ECDH primitive (secp256k1 tweak_mul, since nixpkgs secp lacks the ecdh module) + pubkey recovery, 3/3 tested. REMAINING: AEAD (libsodium bind), epoch/membership/re-key structure, F-16 property test. Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: F-16 epoch encryption (ECIES-secp256k1 wrap, re-key on membership change)

payload.body: ConversationCrypto seam defined (module/src/crypto/conversation.nim) — the swappable boundary per the amended ADR-010: seal/open/addMember/removeMember/members/epoch. Our EpochCrypto (ECIES-secp256k1) will be a labeled stopgap behind it; native logos-chat-module binds here once it ships persistence+removal. Members identified by secp256k1 PubKey (no second curve). Type-checks. REMAINING for the stopgap impl: AEAD (libsodium secretbox bind), ECIES wrap/unwrap (ecdh+AEAD, ecdh primitive already done), the epoch/membership/re-key structure, and the F-16 property test (joiner can't open earlier epochs).

EpochCrypto STOPGAP DONE — F-16 verified in code (5/5). module/src/crypto/sodium.nim (libsodium secretbox AEAD bind, symbols confirmed) + epoch_crypto.nim (ECIES-secp256k1: ephemeral key -> ecdh -> secretbox wraps a per-epoch key to each member's secp256k1 pubkey; per-conversation epochs; re-key on add/remove) behind the ConversationCrypto interface. tests/epoch_crypto_test.nim asserts the F-16 property (the ADR-010 'verify not trust' bar): a member added at epoch 2 CANNOT open an epoch-1 envelope; a removed member CANNOT open a later epoch; a non-recipient can't unwrap a grant. Members = secp256k1 pubkeys (no second curve). Explicitly a stopgap: native chat binds the same interface once it ships persistence+removal. REMAINING (next increment, not this session): wire ConversationCrypto+Transport into the multi-instance coordination flow (publish sealed intent events, ingest+open peer events), add libsodium to the module nix.packages when wired, live two-instance test.

payload.description: Operation-based Keystore interface (sign/ecdh/address/pubKey) so a Keycard/OS-keystore backend can slot behind it later.
